moveStyle.description: Movement style, e.g. Auto, Walk, Run.

specialMove.description: Special move style, e.g. None, LedgeGrab, Roll.

tools.name: randomize_transforms
tools.title: Randomize Transforms
tools.description: Add natural variation to existing objects: random yaw and/or random uniform scale within a range. Great for breaking up repetition in placed foliage/rocks/crates. Seeded — the same seed reproduces the same layout. Returns { randomized, seed } (the count of objects changed); scale only varies when scaleMax > scaleMin.

ids.description: GUIDs of the GameObjects to randomize.

scaleMax.description: Max uniform scale (default 1; set >min to vary).

tools.name: raycast
tools.title: Raycast
tools.description: Perform a physics raycast (Scene.Trace.Ray) from start to end — pass both; the handler traces the start→end segment. Useful for line-of-sight checks, object placement, and collision detection. Returns { hit, hitPosition, normal, distance, gameObjectId, gameObjectName } — feed gameObjectId into get_all_properties/set_transform, or visualize the result with debug_draw_ray. A 'Default Surface not found' error is a known transient; call restart_editor and retry.

start.description: Ray start position (world space) — object {x,y,z} or comma string "x,y,z". As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

end.description: Ray end position. Use either end or direction+maxDistance. As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

direction.description: Ray direction (normalized). Used with maxDistance instead of end. As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

maxDistance.description: Maximum ray distance when using direction. Defaults to 10000.

all.description: If true, returns all hits along the ray. Defaults to false (first hit only).

tools.name: raycast_terrain
tools.title: Raycast Terrain
tools.description: Sample MapBuilder terrain height at world (x, y). Returns z (the surface height). Use to place props on the terrain surface.

id.description: Optional GameObject GUID for MapBuilder.

component.description: Override the terrain component type name (default MapBuilder).

tools.name: razor_lint
tools.title: Razor Lint
tools.description: Static-scan .razor and .razor.scss files for the silent footguns that crash the Razor transpiler or stylesheet engine with no useful error message: switch expressions inside @code blocks (use if/else instead), non-ASCII/emoji inside @code (move to markup or a string constant), PanelComponent subclasses missing a BuildHash override (panel never re-renders), and root uppercase type-selector rules in .razor.scss (silently skipped -- use a class selector like .my-panel). Returns { scanned, findings: [{file, line, match, advice}], clean } matching the sandbox_lint shape.

directory.description: Subdirectory under the project root to scan (e.g. 'UI', 'Code'). Defaults to 'Code'.

tools.name: read_console
tools.title: Read Console
tools.description: Read recent console output, oldest first - what the editor and game logged: prints, warnings, errors, exceptions, compile results. This is how you see the effect of what you just did. Errors come with the top of their stack trace. Every read ends with a cursor - pass it back as 'since' next time to get only what was logged after it, instead of re-reading the same output.

limit.description: How many of the most recent matching entries to return.

filter.description: Only entries whose message or logger name contains this, case insensitive.

since.description: Cursor from a previous read - only entries logged after it come back. 0 reads the most recent.

tools.name: read_file
tools.title: Read File
tools.description: Read the contents of a file in the s&box project (scripts, scenes, configs, etc.).

path.description: Relative path to the file within the project (e.g. 'code/PlayerController.cs').

tools.name: recompile_asset
tools.title: Recompile Asset
tools.description: Compile a project asset by path — registers it with the editor's AssetSystem then compiles it (e.g. .vmat → .vmat_c). Use after writing/editing an asset with write_file so the change takes effect without a manual editor step. Verified on materials. NOTE: the engine exposes no reachable particle (.vpcf) compiler, so this can't compile particles — author those in s&box's particle editor, then spawn_vpcf plays them.

path.description: Asset path — project-relative (e.g. 'materials/foo.vmat') or absolute.

tools.name: record_gameplay_clip
tools.title: Record Gameplay Clip
tools.description: Start recording live play-mode gameplay into a Sandbox.MovieMaker clip — REQUIRES play mode (start_play first; errors otherwise). Captures the given GameObjects (ids — recommended: small focused clips) or, when ids is omitted, the WHOLE scene (heavy: every object becomes tracks). Returns { started, jobId, sampleRate, maxSeconds, capture, discarded, note } immediately; recording runs ASYNC in the editor frame loop until stop_gameplay_recording or the maxSeconds safety cap (default 60s of clip time, max 600s). Only one recording at a time (a second call errors while active; a stopped-but-unsaved clip is discarded by a new start, reported in 'discarded'). Combine with playtest or drive_player to record a SCRIPTED run, then stop_gameplay_recording to save the .movie and play_movie to replay it.

ids.description: GameObject GUIDs to capture (from get_scene_hierarchy WHILE PLAYING — play-mode ids can differ from editor ids). Omit to capture the whole scene (heavy).

maxSeconds.description: Safety cap — auto-stops the recording once the clip timeline reaches this many seconds (default 60, clamped 1-600). The clip stays in memory until stop_gameplay_recording saves it.

tools.name: record_playtest
tools.title: Record Playtest
tools.description: Run a scripted playtest AND record the same run to a .movie clip in ONE call — automated regression footage: a failing playtest comes with a replayable clip of exactly what happened. REQUIRES play mode (start_play first). steps uses the EXACT playtest schema (one verb per step: move / look / lookDelta / action / jump / set / wait / capture / assert — see the playtest tool for the full verb reference). The recording defaults to the playtest's resolved player hierarchy; pass ids to record other objects, or nothing resolvable falls back to whole-scene capture (heavy). Returns { started, steps, recordingJobId, capture, sampleRate, clipName, folder, recorderCapSeconds, note } immediately; both jobs run ASYNC in the editor frame loop and the clip AUTO-SAVES the moment the playtest finishes (a failing or aborted run still saves its footage; play mode ending early is also saved). THE POLL CHAIN: 1) playtest_status until finished:true → the per-step pass/fail transcript. 2) gameplay_recording_status → the saved clip summary { saved, assetPath, durationSeconds, trackCount } (if it still says pendingSave, the save is a frame away — poll again; a save error there means name collision: call stop_gameplay_recording yourself with a new name). Replay the footage with add_movie_player + play_movie. Errors if a playtest or gameplay recording is already active. Only one at a time.

steps.description: Ordered playtest step objects — identical schema to the playtest tool (move/look/lookDelta/action/jump/set/wait/capture/assert). Runs top-to-bottom in the frame loop. JSON array.

id.description: GUID of the player/controller GameObject the playtest drives. Omit to auto-resolve the first PlayerController.

component.description: Controller component type to target (e.g. 'PlayerController'). Omit to auto-detect.

ids.description: GameObject GUIDs to RECORD (from get_scene_hierarchy WHILE PLAYING). Omit to record the playtest's player hierarchy (the default and usually what you want).

clipName.description: Saved .movie asset name without extension (default playtest_<UTC timestamp>; sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_-]).

folder.description: Assets subfolder to save the clip into (default "recordings").

tools.name: redo
tools.title: Redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone edit in the active scene.

tools.name: remove_component
tools.title: Remove Component
tools.description: Remove a component. Give the component's id, or its game object's id plus a type name. The user can undo this. Removal applies at the end of the frame, so reading the object in the same batch still shows it.

id.description: The component's id, or its game object's id.

type.description: The component type to remove, when id is a game object.

tools.name: rename_gameobject
tools.title: Rename Gameobject
tools.description: Change the display name of a GameObject identified by its GUID (the GUID itself never changes, so existing references stay valid). Returns { renamed, id, oldName, newName }. Name-based lookups (e.g. find_objects) will see the new name immediately.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject.

name.description: New display name.

tools.name: replace_model
tools.title: Replace Model
tools.description: Swap the model on one object (id) or many (ids) — e.g. retheme a row of props in one call.

id.description: Single GameObject GUID.

ids.description: Multiple GameObject GUIDs.

tools.name: restart_editor
tools.title: Restart Editor
tools.description: Restart the s&box editor and wait for the bridge to reconnect — closes the C#-edit→recompile loop so addon/bridge changes apply without a manual restart. Relaunches straight back into the current project (EditorUtility.RestartEditor). Saves unsaved scenes by default (pass save:false to discard them). Blocks until the bridge is back (or waitMs elapses), then reports the handler count.

save.description: Save unsaved scenes before restarting (default true; false discards them).

waitMs.description: Max ms to wait for reconnect (default 150000).

tools.name: restore_checkpoint
tools.title: Restore Checkpoint
tools.description: REPLACE the open scene's entire contents with a checkpoint_scene snapshot: destroys every current root object, then rebuilds the snapshot's tree (guids preserved, so internal references stay wired). DESTRUCTIVE — requires an explicit id (from checkpoint_scene or list_checkpoints), never guesses. Returns { restored, id, destroyedRoots, restoredRoots }. The scene FILE on disk is untouched until save_scene. Scene-mutating: refused during play mode.

id.description: Checkpoint id to restore (e.g. 'cp_20260709_153000_before-batch-tint').

tools.name: run_csharp
tools.title: Run
tools.description: Run a trusted C# method body on the engine main thread in game scope. Supply code OR an absolute path to a UTF-8 script file. Supports await and return (object); System, System.Linq, System.Threading, System.Threading.Tasks and Sandbox are imported. Parameters exchangeDirectory and cancellationToken are available. Example: return Game.ActiveScene?.Name; Engine/editor APIs are available, with editor types fully qualified. This has full local process privileges, may mutate live state, and does not create undo steps. Cancellation is cooperative: check cancellationToken in loops. Discover this tool through search_tools.

code.description: C# method body to execute. Mutually exclusive with path.

path.description: Absolute path to a UTF-8 C# method body, usually in the session exchange directory.

tools.name: sandbox_lint
tools.title: Sandbox Lint
tools.description: Static-scan the project's C# for s&box sandbox whitelist violations BEFORE they cause compile errors: System.MathF (use MathX), System.Math (use MathX), Array.Clone() (use .ToArray()), System.Net / raw sockets (use Sandbox.Http), System.IO.File (use FileSystem.Data), and raw System.Threading.Thread (use async/Task or GameTask). Returns { scanned, findings: [{file, line, match, advice}], clean }. Scope to a subdirectory with the directory param.

directory.description: Subdirectory under the project root to scan (e.g. 'Code', 'Code/Player'). Defaults to 'Code'.

tools.name: save_camera_bookmark
tools.title: Save Camera Bookmark
tools.description: Save or replace a named camera bookmark in editor-session memory. Pass targetId to save the bridge's deterministic framed view of a GameObject, position plus lookAt/rotation for an explicit pose, or omit both to snapshot the current main camera. Returns the resolved pose. Bookmarks reset on addon hotload or editor restart; list them with list_camera_bookmarks and capture an ordered group with capture_camera_set.

name.description: Bookmark name (case-insensitive, 1-64 characters).

targetId.description: GameObject GUID to resolve into a deterministic framed pose.

lookAt.description: World point to aim at as "x,y,z"; pair with position.

rotation.description: Explicit camera rotation as "pitch,yaw,roll"; alternative to lookAt.

fov.description: Field of view in degrees (clamped 1-179). Defaults to 80, or the main camera FOV when snapshotting it.

tools.name: save_inspect
tools.title: Save Inspect
tools.description: Inspect the game's FileSystem.Data save files — the assistant is otherwise blind to persisted state. action='list' (default) returns `directories` and `files` [{name, path, size}] under `path` (omit path for the Data root); action='read' returns {path, length, content}, truncating content at 60,000 chars; action='diff' compares two save files key-by-key, returning `diffCount` and up to 200 `diffs` [{key, change: added|removed|changed}]. Use to verify a save actually wrote, debug a load/migration, or confirm a sanitize/clamp ran.

action.description: 'list' (default) enumerates a folder; 'read' dumps one file's JSON; 'diff' compares `path` vs `pathB`. One of: list | read | diff. Default: "list".

path.description: File or folder path under FileSystem.Data (e.g. 'lumber_corp2_progress' or '<folder>/steam_123.json').

tools.name: save_scene
tools.title: Save Scene
tools.description: Save the active scene to its file.

tools.name: scaffold_map_vote_flow
tools.title: Scaffold Map Vote Flow
tools.description: Scaffold an end-of-round map vote. Three files: <Name>.cs (sealed host-authoritative controller) + <Name>Panel.razor + <Name>Panel.razor.scss (vote UI: one button per map, live tallies, countdown, own-pick highlight, winner banner). Flow: host calls StartVote() (usually from a post-round phase/state, or set the AutoStart [Property]) -> clients click -> votes route client-to-host via [Rpc.Host] SubmitVote with the caller re-resolved HOST-SIDE from Rpc.Caller (null-checked — Connection has no IsValid on this SDK) and the map index re-validated (re-votes overwrite, keyed by SteamId) -> tallies replicate via [Sync(FromHost)] NetList<int> -> when the [Sync] TimeUntil countdown expires the host picks the winner (most votes; ties break deterministically via one LCG scramble of a time seed — no System.Random) -> after resultLingerSeconds the HOST calls Scene.LoadFromFile(winner) (API verified live on this SDK; clients follow via the scene networking layer — verify the client hand-off in a real multi-client session). Static event OnVoteFinished(sceneFile) fires on every machine. Returns { created, componentPath, razorPath, scssPath, className, panelClassName, maps, voteDurationSeconds, resultLingerSeconds, autoStart, note, nextSteps }. REQUIREMENTS: the controller must sit on a NETWORK-SPAWNED object in multiplayer or [Sync] never replicates; if maps is omitted the MapScenes list is generated EMPTY and StartVote() refuses with a warning until you fill it in the inspector. Follow with trigger_hotload, attach via add_component_with_properties, host the panel under add_screen_panel.

name.description: Class name for the controller; the panel is generated as <Name>Panel. Defaults to 'MapVote'.

directory.description: Subdirectory for the generated .cs + .razor + .razor.scss. Defaults to 'Code'.

maps.description: Scene files to vote between, e.g. ["scenes/arena.scene", "scenes/docks.scene"] (find them with list_scenes). Baked into the MapScenes [Property] list, editable later in the inspector. Defaults to an EMPTY list (StartVote() then refuses until it's filled).

voteDurationSeconds.description: Seconds the vote stays open once StartVote() is called (clamped to >= 3). Defaults to 20.

resultLingerSeconds.description: Seconds the winner banner shows before the host loads the winning scene (clamped to >= 0). Defaults to 4.

autoStart.description: Start the vote automatically on spawn (host only). Usually false — call StartVote() from your round machine's post-round state instead. Defaults to false.

tools.name: scatter_props
tools.title: Scatter Props
tools.description: Scatter seeded model copies inside a radius. Existing calls mutate immediately and keep the legacy { scattered, groupId, seed } result. Use dryRun:true to resolve random transforms and ground traces once, returning per-slot transforms, ground status, warnings, model bounds, and planId; commit_placement_plan creates exactly that preview with rollback on failure.

center.description: Centre of the scatter area (default origin). As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

randomYaw.description: Randomly rotate each around Z (default true).

snapToGround.description: Raycast each onto the surface below (default true).

scaleMax.description: Max uniform scale (default 1; set >min for size variation).

tint.description: Tint applied to every copy — object {r,g,b,a} or comma string "r,g,b,a". As "r,g,b[,a]" (0-1 floats).

seed.description: PRNG seed for a reproducible layout (default 1).

group.description: Parent all copies under one group object (default true).

name.description: Base name for the props/group (default 'Prop').

dryRun.description: Preview only: return deterministic transforms and planId without creating props.

tools.name: scene_trace
tools.title: Scene Trace
tools.description: Trace a ray through the active scene's physics and report what it hits - find the floor, check line of sight, probe where something can be placed.

StartedSolid.description: Whether the trace started inside something solid.

EndPosition.description: Where the trace ended - the hit point, or the requested end on a miss.

Fraction.description: How far along the ray the hit was, 0 to 1.

Distance.description: How far the trace travelled, in units.

GameObject.description: The game object hit. Null on a miss.

Component.description: The component type hit. Null on a miss.

tools.name: scene_tree
tools.title: Scene Tree
tools.description: The game object hierarchy of an open scene - every object's name, id, enabled state and component types, nested like the editor's hierarchy panel. Use the ids with get_game_object to dig into a specific object.

scene.description: Scene name or resource path from list_scenes. Empty for the active scene.

maxDepth.description: How many levels deep to descend. 0 for unlimited.

Children.description: Child objects. Null when the depth limit or node budget cut them off.

tools.name: scene_validate
tools.title: Scene Validate
tools.description: Validate the active scene for the silent setup footguns that break controllers/physics/cameras: no CameraComponent, no player controller, multiple root Rigidbodies, a Rigidbody with MotionEnabled=false fighting a kinematic root, IsTrigger colliders that Scene.Trace will ignore, child Rigidbodies breaking collider binding, and missing required child anchors. Returns each issue with the GameObject and the exact fix.

tools.name: screenshot_from
tools.title: Screenshot From
tools.description: Frame a GameObject or a free camera position and return the shot as an inline PNG image. Same as capture_view (kept under its historical name — existing workflows use it), with the same capture limits: UI text may rasterise as boxes, and Terrain renders truncated from a temporary camera (clipmap centres on the main camera) — verify terrain via take_screenshot.

id.description: GUID of a GameObject to auto-frame.

lookAt.description: Point to aim the camera at, as "x,y,z".

tools.name: screenshot_orbit
tools.title: Screenshot Orbit
tools.description: Capture a GameObject from several angles in ONE call — orbits around the object and returns every angle as an inline PNG image, so 3D work can be verified from multiple sides instead of guessed from one. Temporary-camera limits apply: Terrain renders as a truncated ribbon (clipmap centres on the main camera) and UI text may rasterise as boxes.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject to orbit.

shots.description: Number of angles around the object (2-8). Default 4.

elevation.description: Camera height factor: 0 = level with the object, 1 = high above. Default 0.4.

distance.description: Camera distance in units. Default: auto from the object's bounds.

tools.name: sculpt_terrain
tools.title: Sculpt Terrain
tools.description: Apply a heightmap brush at (x, y) to MapBuilder. Modes: raise, lower, flatten, smooth. Modifies the current heightmap directly and rebuilds the mesh; edits survive between calls but are lost when 'Build Terrain' regenerates from the feature lists. Returns `sculpted`, `mode`, and `affected_vertices`; verify with raycast_terrain at the brush center.

strength.description: Height delta (units) for raise/lower; ignored for flatten/smooth.

mode.description: Brush mode. Default 'raise'. `strength` applies to raise/lower only. One of: raise | lower | flatten | smooth. Default: "raise".

id.description: GUID of the GameObject holding the MapBuilder; omit to auto-find the first MapBuilder in the scene.

component.description: Override the builder component type name — set this if your project's terrain/cave/forest component is named differently than the default (MapBuilder/CaveBuilder/ForestGenerator).

tools.name: search_assets
tools.title: Search Assets
tools.description: Search for assets in the project by name, type, or keyword. Returns models, materials, sounds, textures, prefabs, etc.

query.description: Search term to match against asset name or path.

maxResults.description: Maximum results to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.title: Search Tools
tools.description: Search the live tool registry. Tools live in editor and addon code and come and go as code hotloads, so the tool list from when you connected can be stale - this one never is. Every keyword must match the name, description or parameters; empty returns every tool. Invoke anything you find with call_tool.

query.description: Space separated keywords. Empty for every tool.

tools.name: search_types
tools.title: Search Types
tools.description: Find loaded types matching a name pattern. Useful for discovering 'is there a built-in X for this?'. Returns `count` and `matches` with each type's name, fullName, isComponent, and isAbstract — results are silently truncated at `limit` (default 50), so narrow the pattern if you hit the cap. Pass a match's name to describe_type for its full member surface.

pattern.description: Substring to match against type name (case-insensitive).

limit.description: Maximum matches to return (default 50); the search stops silently at this cap.

tools.name: select_object
tools.title: Select Object
tools.description: Select a GameObject in the editor (highlights it in the hierarchy and scene view). Replaces the current selection unless addToSelection=true. Returns { selected, id }; confirm the result with get_selected_objects.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject to select.

addToSelection.description: If true, adds to current selection instead of replacing it.

tools.name: services_query
tools.title: Services Query
tools.description: Read from Sandbox.Services — the cloud stats/leaderboard layer many games use as their real DB. action='stats' with `name` returns the local player's stat {ident, value, sum, min, max, lastValue, valueString}; without `name` it returns only the package ident plus a usage note (it does NOT list stat definitions). action='leaderboard' (name required) returns {board, displayName, totalEntries, count, entries} with at most `limit` entries (default 10). Read-only; use to verify a Stats.Increment/SetValue path or a leaderboard wired correctly.

action.description: 'stats' (default) reads a local-player stat by `name`; 'leaderboard' fetches a board's top entries. One of: stats | leaderboard. Default: "stats".

name.description: Stat name (action='stats') or leaderboard/board name (action='leaderboard').

tools.name: set_animgraph_param
tools.title: Set Animgraph Param
tools.description: Set an AnimationGraph parameter on a GameObject's SkinnedModelRenderer (calls Set). This drives Citizen/animgraph motion — e.g. 'move_x'/'move_y' (float), 'b_grounded'/'b_ducked' (bool), or a Vector3. Pose previews in-editor when PlayAnimationsInEditorScene is on; screenshot to verify. Param names are defined by the model's animation graph — use list_animations to check whether the model is animgraph-driven. Returns { set, param, kind, note } — kind is the type actually applied (float/int/bool/vector).

id.description: GUID of the GameObject with a SkinnedModelRenderer.

value.description: Value: number (float), boolean, or a vector as {x,y,z} OR a comma string "x,y,z". As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

type.description: Force the parameter type (default: inferred from value). One of: float | int | bool | vector.

tools.name: set_bodygroup
tools.title: Set Bodygroup
tools.description: Show/hide a bodygroup on a SkinnedModelRenderer (e.g. hide hands when holding a tool, swap head variants). Provide value (int index) or choice (string name). Returns { set, bodygroup } on success (errors if the object has no SkinnedModelRenderer or neither value nor choice is given); take_screenshot to verify the visual change.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject with a SkinnedModelRenderer.

name.description: Bodygroup name.

choice.description: Bodygroup choice by name (alternative to value).

tools.name: set_component
tools.title: Set Component
tools.description: Set properties on a component. Give the component's id, or its game object's id plus a type name. Values use the same serialized forms get_game_object shows - strings, numbers, 'x,y,z' vectors, colors as 'r,g,b,a', asset paths as strings. Everything validates before anything applies, and the user can undo it.

id.description: The component's id, or its game object's id.

properties.description: A json object of property name to new value.

type.description: The component type to change, when id is a game object.

tools.name: set_component_reference
tools.title: Set Component Reference
tools.description: Wire a component's GameObject/Component-typed property to ANOTHER live object in the scene by GUID (e.g. ObjectiveManager.Player = the player, a camera's follow target, a door's hinge). Preferred for object/component refs (can pick a specific component type off the target via targetComponent, and validates). set_property also accepts a GUID for ref props; set_prefab_ref is for prefab assets. Set clear:true to null the reference.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject that HOLDS the component you're writing into.

component.description: Component type name on that object (e.g. 'ObjectiveManager', 'CameraComponent').

property.description: The property to set (must be a GameObject- or Component-typed property).

targetId.description: GUID of the GameObject to reference. Required unless clear:true.

targetComponent.description: If the property is a Component subtype, the specific component type to pull off the target object. Omit to auto-match by the property's type.

clear.description: If true, set the reference to null instead of assigning a target.

tools.name: set_editor_camera
tools.title: Set Editor Camera
tools.description: Move the editor scene camera. Give a position and/or angles - anything left empty keeps its current value. Returns the resulting transform.

tools.name: set_enabled
tools.title: Set Enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a GameObject (disabled objects are invisible and inactive, including their components and children). Returns { id, enabled } confirming the new state.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject.

enabled.description: true to enable, false to disable.

tools.name: set_expression
tools.title: Set Expression
tools.description: Set a facial morph (blendshape) on a skinned model — e.g. smile, frown, blink. Call with NO morph to list the model's available morph names (returned as availableMorphs). weight is typically 0-1. Returns { set, morph, weight, availableMorphs } — availableMorphs is included in every response, so a wrong name can be corrected without an extra listing call.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject with a SkinnedModelRenderer.

morph.description: Morph/blendshape name (omit to list available morphs).

tools.name: set_fog
tools.title: Set Fog
tools.description: Add or update fog in the active scene. Types: 'gradient' (distance haze — great for mood/horror), 'cubemap' (sky-tinted distance fog), 'volumetric' (a localized fog volume). Re-running with the same targetId updates it rather than duplicating; without targetId each call creates a new fog object. Returns { created, type, gameObject } — gameObject.id addresses the fog object for later set_property/delete_gameobject; screenshot to verify the look.

type.description: Fog type (default gradient). One of: gradient | cubemap | volumetric.

name.description: GameObject name when creating a new fog object.

targetId.description: GUID of an existing GameObject to host the fog (else a new fog object is created).

color.description: Fog colour (gradient/volumetric Color, cubemap Tint). As "r,g,b[,a]" (0-1 floats).

endDistance.description: gradient/cubemap: distance (units) where fog reaches full density.

height.description: gradient: world height the fog settles around.

heightStart.description: cubemap: world height where height-fog starts.

size.description: volumetric: bounds size (units) centred on the object — object {x,y,z} or comma string "x,y,z". As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

tools.name: set_forest_seed
tools.title: Set Forest Seed
tools.description: Set ForestGenerator.Seed and (by default) regenerate — re-rolls the forest layout while keeping POIs, trails, and density regions. Returns `set`, `seed`, and `rebuilt`; take a screenshot afterwards (screenshot_from) to judge the new layout.

rebuild.description: Regenerate the forest after setting (default true).

id.description: GUID of the GameObject holding the ForestGenerator; omit to auto-find the first ForestGenerator in the scene.

component.description: Override the builder component type name — set this if your project's terrain/cave/forest component is named differently than the default (MapBuilder/CaveBuilder/ForestGenerator).

tools.name: set_game_object
tools.title: Set Game Object
tools.description: Change a game object - rename, enable/disable, reparent, move, rotate or scale. Only the arguments you give change; everything else stays. The user can undo this.

id.description: The game object's id, from scene_tree or find_game_objects.

name.description: New name.

parent.description: New parent game object id, or 'root' for the scene root.

scale.description: Scale as 'x,y,z', or a single number for uniform.

Parent.description: The parent. Null when parented to the scene root.

tools.name: set_look_at
tools.title: Set Look At
tools.description: Aim a Citizen's gaze. Pass target {x,y,z} (spawns a LookTarget) or targetId (existing GameObject) and the head/eyes track it. Pass enabled:false to turn gaze tracking off. Tune eyesWeight/headWeight/bodyWeight (0-1).

id.description: GUID of the Citizen (must have a CitizenAnimationHelper).

target.description: World point to look at. As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

targetId.description: GUID of a GameObject to look at (overrides target).

tools.name: set_material_property
tools.title: Set Material Property
tools.description: Change a property on the material assigned to a GameObject — color, roughness, metallic, texture, etc. Operates on the ModelRenderer's MaterialOverride; if none is assigned it auto-creates one from the default complex shader (no separate assign_material step needed). Returns { set, id, property, autoCreatedMaterial } — screenshot to verify the visual change.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject.

value.description: Property value — number for floats, string for texture paths/colors, {r,g,b,a} for colors. JSON value.

tools.name: set_ownership
tools.title: Set Ownership
tools.description: Assign network ownership of a GameObject to a connection, or drop ownership. Omitting connectionId (or passing an empty string) calls Network.DropOwnership(); passing a connection Id or SteamId calls Network.AssignOwnership() on the matching live Connection. Returns { ownershipAssigned, id, connectionId } or { ownershipDropped, id }; errors if no connection matches (connections only exist while networking is active).

id.description: GUID of the networked GameObject.

connectionId.description: Connection Id GUID or SteamId of the target connection. Omit OR pass an empty string to DROP ownership (there is no take-ownership mode in the current handler).

tools.name: set_parent
tools.title: Set Parent
tools.description: Reparent a GameObject. Set parentId to null or omit to move to scene root.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject to reparent.

parentId.description: GUID of the new parent. Null or omitted = scene root.

tools.name: set_prefab_ref
tools.title: Set Prefab Ref
tools.description: Set a GameObject-typed property on a component to a loaded prefab. Use this when set_property can't handle prefab references (which it can't, because prefabs are GameObjects not primitives).

id.description: GUID of the GameObject holding the component.

component.description: Component type name.

property.description: Property name to set (must be GameObject-typed).

tools.name: set_project_config
tools.title: Set Project Config
tools.description: Update project configuration fields for publishing: title, description, version, type, package ident, summary, visibility. Only provided fields are changed — edits string values in the .sbproj file in place. Returns { updated, path } (the .sbproj path); read the result back with get_project_config to confirm what actually changed.

isPublic.description: Whether the project is publicly visible.

tools.name: set_project_thumbnail
tools.title: Set Project Thumbnail
tools.description: Set or update the project thumbnail image (thumb.png) used for publishing. Provide either a source path or base64 image data.

sourcePath.description: Relative path to an image file within the project to use as thumbnail.

base64.description: Base64-encoded image data to write as thumbnail.

format.description: Image format when using base64 mode. Defaults to 'png'. One of: png | jpg.

tools.name: set_property
tools.title: Set Property
tools.description: Set a property value on a component (editor mode), and PERSIST it (survives save+reload). Handles primitives, enums, value types (Color/Vector3 as comma strings), AND references: pass an asset PATH for Model/Material/Texture/SoundEvent props, or a GameObject GUID for GameObject/Component-typed props (resolved like set_component_reference). Returns success=false with a clear error if a path/GUID can't be resolved (no more silent null). For wiring object refs prefer set_component_reference; for prefab refs use set_prefab_ref.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject.

component.description: Component type name.

value.description: New value. Primitive: '5', 'true'. Color/Vector3: a comma string ('1,0,0,1' / '0,0,200'), an array ([0,0,200]), or an object ({r,g,b,a} / {x,y,z}). Enum: the member name. Asset ref (Model/Material/...): the asset path e.g. 'models/dev/box.vmdl'. GameObject/Component ref: the target GameObject's GUID. Empty/'null' clears the property. JSON value.

tools.name: set_runtime_property
tools.title: Set Runtime Property
tools.description: Set a component property value during play mode — tweak values live while the game runs. Errors if the game is not playing (start_play first). Returns { set, id, component, property, value } like set_property; read it back with get_runtime_property. Runtime changes are DISCARDED when play mode stops — use set_property in edit mode to persist.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject.

component.description: Component type name.

tools.name: set_selection
tools.title: Set Selection
tools.description: Replace the editor selection. Selecting something highlights it for the user - useful for showing them what you're talking about. An empty list clears the selection.

ids.description: Game object or component ids to select.

tools.name: set_skybox
tools.title: Set Skybox
tools.description: Set the scene's 2D skybox tint / indirect lighting (re-uses an existing SkyBox2D or creates one). Darken the tint for night/dusk. Optionally point it at a .vmat sky material (silently kept as-is if the material fails to load). Returns { created, gameObject } — gameObject.id is the sky object; screenshot to verify the change.

indirectLighting.description: Whether the sky contributes indirect/ambient light.

name.description: Name for the sky GameObject if one is created.

tools.name: set_tags
tools.title: Set Tags
tools.description: Add, remove, and/or clear gameplay tags on one object (id) or many (ids). Tags drive collision groups, queries, and triggers.

id.description: Single GameObject GUID.

ids.description: Multiple GameObject GUIDs.

tools.name: set_time_scale
tools.title: Set Time Scale
tools.description: Set the running game's time scale DURING PLAY MODE (ported from Unity's playtest_set_time_scale). 0 = pause, 1 = normal, 0.1 = slow-mo to watch a fast interaction frame-by-frame, 2+ = fast-forward idle/economy ticks. Requires start_play first — the edit scene doesn't tick, so this no-ops outside play mode and returns an error. Sets Game.ActiveScene.TimeScale (clamped to 0–100). Returns the applied and previous values.

scale.description: Time multiplier: 0 = pause, 1 = normal speed, 0.1 = slow-mo, 2 = double speed. Clamped to 0–100.

tools.name: set_tint
tools.title: Set Tint
tools.description: Set the renderer tint colour on one object (id) or many (ids) at once. Works on any ModelRenderer/SkinnedModelRenderer. Pass the colour as "tint" (or its alias "color"); each accepts an object {r,g,b,a} OR a comma string "r,g,b,a".

id.description: Single GameObject GUID.

ids.description: Multiple GameObject GUIDs.

tint.description: Tint colour to apply (object or comma string). As "r,g,b[,a]" (0-1 floats).

color.description: Alias for "tint" (object or comma string). As "r,g,b[,a]" (0-1 floats).

tools.name: set_transform
tools.title: Set Transform
tools.description: Atomically set position, rotation, and/or scale on a GameObject. All supplied values are parsed before mutation; values apply in world space by default. Prefer space='local' or space='world'; local remains a legacy alias. Returns legacy { transformed, gameObject } plus before/after transform and bounds receipts.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject.

scale.description: New scale — uniform number, per-axis object {x,y,z}, or comma string "x,y,z". As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

local.description: Legacy alias: true selects local space and false selects world space.

space.description: Explicit transform space. If supplied with local, both values must agree. One of: world | local.

tools.name: simulate_input
tools.title: Simulate Input
tools.description: Press or release a named input action during PLAY mode (via Sandbox.Input.SetAction) so input-driven behavior — jump, attack1, use, reload, IPressable, weapon fire — can be verified without a human at the keyboard. REQUIRES play mode and a named `action`; returns {action, state: 'down'|'up', note}. Caveats: SetAction applies to the current input frame ('press' and 'hold' both set the action down; 'release' clears it), and analogMove/analogLook/durationMs are accepted but IGNORED — Sandbox.Input has no analog injection API, so for movement use drive_player or the playtest harness instead.

action.description: Named input action to drive (must exist in Input.config), e.g. 'jump', 'attack1', 'use'.

state.description: press = one tick (Pressed); hold = held for durationMs; release = clear a held action. One of: press | hold | release. Default: "press".

analogMove.description: AnalogMove vector to apply (forward/left) -- object {x,y,z} or comma string "x,y,z". As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

analogLook.description: AnalogLook angles delta to apply. As "pitch,yaw,roll" degrees.

durationMs.description: How long to hold the action / apply the analog values.

tools.name: simulate_npc_perception
tools.title: Simulate Npc Perception
tools.description: READ-ONLY edit-mode verifier: evaluate the NPC's perception math RIGHT NOW without entering play mode. Given an NPC (reads its NpcBrain SightRange/FovDegrees/EyeHeight/TargetTag + transform) and either a targetId or a point, it runs the SAME line-of-sight check the brain uses — FOV cone (dot vs the baked cosine), sight-range gate, and an occlusion trace from the eye to the target — and reports the result AND why. This is the keystone verifier: it makes the perception layer checkable in edit mode (no flaky screenshot timing) — e.g. place the Sasquatch, place a camper behind a tree, and confirm the tree blocks LOS. Call params override the brain's values, so it also works before/without an NpcBrain (uses defaults). Safe in play mode too (read-only, like raycast).

npcId.description: GUID of the NPC GameObject (ideally with an NpcBrain; its perception [Property] values are read).

targetId.description: GUID of the target GameObject to test visibility to (e.g. a player). Provide this OR point.

point.description: A raw world point to test visibility to. Provide this OR targetId. As "x,y,z" (or JSON {x,y,z}).

sightRange.description: Override the sight range for this check (else read from the NpcBrain / default 1500).

fovDegrees.description: Override the FOV cone angle for this check (else read from the NpcBrain / default 110).

eyeHeight.description: Override the eye height for this check (else read from the NpcBrain / default 64).

targetTag.description: Override the target tag (canSee also requires the target to carry this tag; else read from the NpcBrain / default 'player').

tools.name: snap_to_ground
tools.title: Snap To Ground
tools.description: Drop a GameObject straight down onto the surface below it (physics raycast). Works best on collider-less props (an object with its own collider may self-hit). Optional offset lifts it off the surface. Returns { snapped, groundZ, gameObject } with the object's updated transform — or { snapped: false, reason } (not an error) when no ground was hit below.

id.description: GUID of the GameObject to snap.

offset.description: Height above the surface to place it (default 0).

startHeight.description: How far above the object to start the trace (default 2000).

tools.name: spawn_citizen
tools.title: Spawn Citizen
tools.description: Spawn an animated Citizen character: a SkinnedModelRenderer with the Citizen model, plus (by default) a CitizenAnimationHelper so it idles. PlayAnimationsInEditorScene is enabled so the idle pose shows in the editor view (screenshot-verifiable). Returns { created, hasAnimator, gameObject:{ id, name, position, components, ... } } — pass gameObject.id to the follow-ups: dress_citizen, pose_citizen, set_expression, equip_model.

name.description: GameObject name (default 'Citizen').

animator.description: Add a CitizenAnimationHelper for idle/pose (default true).

holdType.description: Initial hold pose, e.g. None, Pistol, Rifle, Shotgun, HoldItem, Punch, Swing.

moveStyle.description: Movement style, e.g. Auto, Walk, Run.

tools.name: spawn_model
tools.title: Spawn Model
tools.description: Create a game object with a ModelRenderer in one call - the fastest way to put a model in the scene. Optionally tint it, override its material, scale it and parent it. The user can undo this. Returns the new object's id.

name.description: The new object's name. Empty uses the model filename.

scale.description: Scale as 'x,y,z', or a single number for uniform.

material.description: Material asset path to override every surface with.

parent.description: Parent game object id. Empty parents to the scene root.

tools.name: spawn_models
tools.title: Spawn Models
tools.description: Create many model game objects in one call - each item takes the same fields spawn_model does. Use this to build big arrangements without a round trip per object. One undo step covers the whole batch. Returns the created ids.

Name.description: The new object's name. Empty uses the model filename.

Scale.description: Scale as 'x,y,z', or a single number for uniform.

Material.description: Material asset path to override every surface with.

Parent.description: Parent game object id. Empty parents to the scene root.

tools.name: spawn_particle
tools.title: Spawn Particle
tools.description: EXPERIMENTAL — build an additive runtime ParticleEffect (no texture asset needed): kind = fire, embers, sparks, magic, dust, blood, or snow ('smoke' returns an error). Returns { created, kind, gameObject } — the component graph is created, but this runtime particle path has NOT been verified to render through the bridge; for particles you can actually see, prefer spawn_vpcf.

kind.description: Particle preset. One of: fire | embers | sparks | magic | dust | blood | snow.

color.description: Override the particle tint. As "r,g,b[,a]" (0-1 floats).

name.description: GameObject name.

tools.name: spawn_vpcf
tools.title: Spawn Vpcf
tools.description: Spawn a REAL particle system by playing a compiled .vpcf asset through LegacyParticleSystem — the reliable path that actually renders, unlike spawn_particle/create_particle_effect (which build a runtime ParticleEffect graph that shows nothing). Defaults to 'particles/impact.generic.vpcf' (a sparks/impact burst — the only particle .vpcf reliably present; set looped + a warm tint for a fire-ish effect). Pass your own compiled .vpcf logical path if you have one. Screenshot-verifiable in edit mode.

vpcf.description: Logical .vpcf path (default 'particles/impact.generic.vpcf'). NOT the .vpcf_c or .sbox/cloud cache path.

name.description: GameObject name.

tint.description: Color tint (e.g. orange for fire); applied to the live SceneObject if it's ready this frame. As "r,g,b[,a]" (0-1 floats).

tools.name: start_multiplayer_test
tools.title: Start Multiplayer Test
tools.description: Start a real local multiplayer test from PLAY MODE. Creates an explicitly private, hidden lobby when needed, validates capacity, launches 1-2 sbox.exe clients with -joinlocal, and tracks joins from the pre-spawn host-side connection baseline. Overlapping tracked runs are rejected so unrelated connections cannot falsely satisfy a join wait. Each client can use about 4.5 GB RAM and take about 80 seconds to join. Returns spawned PIDs, baseline/expected connection counts, and an optional join-wait job; poll multiplayer_test_status and always finish with stop_multiplayer_test.

clients.description: Real client processes to launch (default 1; hard cap 2 per run; stop an existing tracked run first).

maxPlayers.description: Lobby capacity when this call creates it (default 4; must fit the host plus all requested clients). Existing lobby capacity is validated instead.

waitForJoinSeconds.description: Host-side join-wait timeout (default 120; 0 returns immediately after launch).

tools.name: start_play
tools.title: Start Play
tools.description: Enter play mode — starts running the game in the editor. Scripts execute, physics simulate, everything goes live. Returns { started, method } (method 'EditorScene.Play', or 'SetPlaying (fallback)' with editorErrorSkipped when the safe path failed). While playing, scene-mutating tools refuse — use get/set_runtime_property, capture_view, and playtest, then stop_play to edit again.

tools.name: stop_gameplay_recording
tools.title: Stop Gameplay Recording
tools.description: Stop the active gameplay recording and persist it as a project .movie asset the editor can load (written to Assets/<folder>/<name>.movie, registered + compiled — list_movies then shows it with hasCompiledClip). Also saves a job that already auto-stopped (maxSeconds cap, or play mode ended). Returns { saved, assetPath, durationSeconds, trackCount, sampleRate, compiled, stopReason, wired, note } — a trackCount of 0 means nothing was captured and the response warns about it. Pass wireToId to auto-wire a MoviePlayer on that GameObject pointed at the new clip (during play mode that wiring is RUNTIME-ONLY and discarded on stop_play; the .movie asset itself always persists). Errors if the target file already exists (the clip stays in memory — retry with another name). discard:true throws the recording away instead. Replay: add_movie_player + play_movie in play mode.

name.description: Asset name without extension (default recording_<UTC timestamp>; sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_-]).

wireToId.description: GameObject GUID to auto-wire a MoviePlayer at the new clip (runtime-only if done during play mode).

discard.description: Throw the recording away instead of saving it.

tools.name: stop_movie
tools.title: Stop Movie
tools.description: Stop MoviePlayer playback (the counterpart to play_movie). Targets the MoviePlayer on the given GameObject, or the first MoviePlayer in the scene when id is omitted. Pass rewind to also reset the playhead to 0 so the next play_movie starts from the top. Works during play mode.

id.description: GameObject GUID holding the MoviePlayer. Omit to use the first MoviePlayer in the scene.

tools.name: stop_multiplayer_test
tools.title: Stop Multiplayer Test
tools.description: Stop every client process launched by start_multiplayer_test; exited clients are cleared while failed live kills remain tracked for retry. Optionally disconnect the host lobby. alsoStrays is an explicit recovery switch that kills every sbox.exe game client, including clients not launched by this harness; it never targets the sbox-dev editor process. Returns truthful stopped/remainingPids, per-process cleanup results, and disconnect status.

disconnect.description: Also disconnect the running host from its networking session (default false).

alsoStrays.description: Also kill untracked sbox.exe game clients (default false; use only for explicit cleanup).

tools.name: stop_play
tools.title: Stop Play
tools.description: Exit play mode — stops the game and returns to editor. All runtime changes are discarded.

tools.name: switch_scene
tools.title: Switch Scene
tools.description: Switch to an already open scene tab, by name or resource path. list_scenes says what's open.

scene.description: Scene name or resource path, as list_scenes reports it.

tools.name: take_screenshot
tools.title: Take Screenshot
tools.description: Screenshot the scene's main camera view (the player's view in play mode) and return it as an inline PNG image. To frame a specific object or position instead, use capture_view or screenshot_orbit. KNOWN CAPTURE LIMIT (engine, not bridge): text in ScreenPanel/Razor labels may rasterise as solid boxes while images and layout are correct — a blank HUD in a capture is NOT a HUD bug; verify text another way (e.g. a Log.Info of the bound value).

renderUI.description: Include screen-space UI (HUD) in the capture. Default true.

tools.name: text_measure
tools.title: Text Measure
tools.description: What a piece of text measures to, through the same text stack the UI draws with. Give a wrap width to measure it wrapped - Lines is how many lines it came out as.

font.description: Font family name, e.g. 'Poppins'. Unknown fonts fall back silently.

lineHeight.description: Line height as a multiple of the font size.

wrapWidth.description: Width to wrap at, in pixels. 0 measures a single line.

tools.name: trigger_hotload
tools.title: Trigger Hotload
tools.description: Nudge s&box to recompile and hotload the project's C# (bumps the .csproj timestamps the file-watcher keys on). NOT synchronous: the compile lands on a later frame, and editing an EXISTING .cs can leave the OLD assembly running silently. Returns { triggered, touched, assemblyBefore, note } — assemblyBefore is the current game-assembly fingerprint; poll get_bridge_status.gameAssembly until it differs (or verify with an explicit marker such as a version string in a Log.Info) BEFORE trusting invoke_button / describe_type output. Falls back to restart_editor for new package dependencies.

tools.name: tune_vehicle
tools.title: Tune Vehicle
tools.description: Apply a handling preset to a vehicle component on a GameObject: arcade (forgiving), drift (low grip, sharp steering), offroad (soft long-travel suspension), or race (fast, planted). Sets EngineForce/MaxSpeed/SteerStrength/GripFactor/SuspensionStrength/SuspensionDamping by name via reflection — targets create_vehicle_controller scaffolds out of the box, partially tunes anything exposing those property names. Returns { tuned, preset, component, applied, missing } — missing lists properties the component lacks. Auto-finds the first component with 'Vehicle' in its type name; pass component to target explicitly. Scene-mutating: refused during play mode (use set_property on runtime objects while playing).

id.description: GUID of the GameObject carrying the vehicle component (from find_objects).

preset.description: Handling preset to apply. One of: arcade | drift | offroad | race.

component.description: Component type name to tune. Default: first component with 'Vehicle' in its name.

tools.name: ui_batch_stats
tools.title: Batch Stats
tools.description: Each root panel's statistics from its last render: timings, panels, draw calls and instances. Instances per draw call is the number that matters: a batch breaks whenever the blend mode changes between boxes, so anything that draws with its own blend mode splits the run it sits in.

tools.name: ui_hit_test
tools.title: Hit Test
tools.description: Which panels are under a point on screen, topmost first. This asks the same question input does, corner radii and all, so it answers both "would a click land here" and "what is eating my clicks" - the first hit whose pointer-events isn't None is the one that takes it.

tools.name: ui_matched_rules
tools.title: Matched Rules
tools.description: Every style rule that matched a panel, in the order the style system applied them - so for any property, the last rule to set it is the one that won. Each rule reports its selector, the file and line it came from, and its declarations. Anything set on the panel directly comes back as Inline, which beats all of them. This is how you find out why a panel doesn't look like the css you wrote.

panel.description: Panel path from ui_panel_dump, or a selector. Empty uses the first root.

tools.name: ui_panel_dump
tools.title: Panel Dump
tools.description: The panel tree with each panel's screen rect, like a browser's elements pane. Every panel comes back with a path, which is how the rest of these tools address it. UI only exists while the scene runs, so play_start first.

panel.description: Panel path like '0/3/1', or a selector like '.mainmenu button'. Empty starts at the roots.

depth.description: How many levels of children to include. ChildCount says what's below the cut.

styles.description: Include the computed style. Every property that's set, so ask for one panel.

styleFilter.description: Only computed properties whose name contains this, e.g. 'border' or 'font'.

tools.name: ui_pixels
tools.title: Pixels
tools.description: Read exact pixel values out of a panel - the numbers behind ui_screenshot, for when looking at an image isn't an answer. Points are relative to the panel's top left, which is what makes them comparable to a browser's readout of the same case. Values are 0-255, straight off the rendered frame.

panel.description: Panel path from ui_panel_dump, or a selector. Empty uses the first root.

points.description: Points to read, as 'x,y x,y x,y'. Empty reads the panel's centre.

tools.name: ui_probe
tools.title: Probe
tools.description: Draw a scratch panel with the css you give it, measure it, screenshot it, then throw it away. This is how you try a declaration without editing a file and waiting for a hotload - state a case, see what it renders to, compare it against a browser. The sample is a 100x100 block, or a label when you give it text, both inset in a cell like tools/uiparity draws them.

css.description: The css to try, e.g. 'border-radius: 20px; background-color: #e8b04a'.

text.description: Text to draw, which makes the sample a label instead of a block.

background.description: Colour behind the sample, so anything with alpha reads against something known.

points.description: Pixels to read, as 'x,y x,y' relative to the sample. Empty reads its centre.

screenshot.description: Return an image as well as the numbers.

tools.name: ui_probe_batch
tools.title: Probe Batch
tools.description: Probe a whole list of css cases at once - one cell each, laid out in a grid, measured together and captured as a single contact sheet. This is the parity sweep: state the cases, get every measurement back in one call, then diff them against the same cases in a browser.

cases.description: One css case per line. Lines starting with # are ignored, so a case file pastes straight in.

text.description: Text to draw, which makes every sample a label instead of a block.

columns.description: Cells per row. 0 fits as many as the screen holds.

points.description: Pixels to read from every sample, as 'x,y x,y'. Empty reads their centres.

screenshot.description: Return the contact sheet as well as the numbers.

tools.name: ui_screenshot
tools.title: Screenshot
tools.description: A screenshot of one panel, cropped to its screen rect, so you can look at what a panel actually draws without hunting for it in a full frame. Renders through the running scene's camera.

panel.description: Panel path from ui_panel_dump, or a selector. Empty uses the first root.

padding.description: Extra pixels around the panel, for seeing shadows and outlines.

tools.name: ui_set_pseudo
tools.title: Set Pseudo
tools.description: Force a pseudo class on a panel - hover, active, focus - so its styles can be looked at and screenshotted without a mouse. Clears again with on false.

panel.description: Panel path from ui_panel_dump, or a selector.

tools.name: ui_set_style
tools.title: Set Style
tools.description: Set css on a live panel, the way a browser's style editor does - change it, look at it, change it again, with no file edit and no hotload in between. This is an inline style, so it beats every rule that matched and it stays until that panel rebuilds. There's no way to take a declaration back off a panel - 'revert' drops it to the initial value, like the web, not back to what the stylesheet said - so put the original value back yourself, or use ui_probe when you want something that cleans up after itself.

panel.description: Panel path from ui_panel_dump, or a selector.

tools.name: undo
tools.title: Undo
tools.description: Undo the last edit in the active scene, exactly like the user pressing ctrl+z. Use it to back out of your own mistake.

tools.name: validate_project
tools.title: Validate Project
tools.description: Validate that the project is ready for publishing. Runs four checks: .sbproj exists, at least one scene, project Ident set, project Title set. Returns { valid, issueCount, issues, checks } — issues are human-readable problems and each checks entry has { check, pass, detail }; fix metadata gaps with set_project_config (it does NOT check compile errors — use get_compile_errors for that).

tools.name: write_file
tools.title: Write File
tools.description: Write or overwrite a file in the s&box project (SILENTLY replaces existing content — read_file first if you need to preserve it). Creates parent directories as needed; paths are confined to the project root (traversal outside it is denied). Returns a confirmation with the path — for C# follow with trigger_hotload so it compiles; for assets (.vmat etc.) follow with recompile_asset.

path.description: Relative path for the file (e.g. 'code/Components/Health.cs').

content.description: The full file content to write.
